fields.narrative_intro: *A grimacing person and a haggard person discuss PostgreSQL 19 in a data center during a fire drill.*
fields.panel1:
[setup]
GRIMACING PERSON: "PostgreSQL 19 was nearly ready."
HAGGARD PERSON: "Then LLM-assisted code reviewers found roughly 40 defects."
fields.panel2:
[build]
HAGGARD PERSON: "The quality bar rose retroactively, says EDB's Peter Eisentraut."
GRIMACING PERSON: "Volunteer maintainers need six-to-eight weeks."
fields.panel3:
[pivot]
GRIMACING PERSON: "Release day is November 19."
HAGGARD PERSON: "Eight-to-ten major features, including SQL/PGQ graph queries, move to PostgreSQL 20."
fields.panel4:
[silent reaction]
[Visual: A red bar blasts through the ceiling as forty paper reports bury the maintainers; tiny AI reviewers keep measuring it upward.]
fields.panel5:
[punch]
HAGGARD PERSON: "Tom Lane says shipping locks bugs in until v20."
GRIMACING PERSON: "So the bugs get tenure before the humans do?"
fields.panel6:
[button]
[Visual: Forty bugs wearing employee lanyards march toward the only exit; the evacuation arrow points into a room labeled “POSTGRESQL 20.”]

narrative_summary: AI review raises PostgreSQL 19's quality bar so high that bugs get promoted and everyone is routed to PostgreSQL 20.
rationale: Candidate 5 turns the story's exact facts—40 defects, the raised quality bar, and features moving to PostgreSQL 20—into a clean, strongly matched visual gag. “The bugs get tenure before the humans do?” is the freshest closing line, and the lanyard-wearing bugs provide an effective button rather than merely repeating the delay.
story_title: Postgres 19 delayed after AI reviewers find more bugs than humans can fix
place: in a data center during a fire drill
hat_pair: foam filing cabinet worn as a tall hat with tiny overflowing drawers
